page: Microsoft Azure D96s_v7 is a high-capacity general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C hardware running up to 4.2 GHz, providing 96 virtual cores derived from 48 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory totals 384.0 GB, which preserves a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. Cache resources are extensive, incorporating 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 480 MB of shared L3 cache. The CPU features hardware acceleration instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX tile and INT8 extensions, and specialized cryptographic extensions.

The D96s_v7 instance includes no local storage drives and no dedicated graphics accelerators. Workloads requiring persistent storage must utilize Azure remote network or premium managed disks. The lack of integrated ephemeral NVMe storage reduces local scratch space but simplifies state management by centralizing disk IO on managed volumes. For compute efficiency, the large 480 MB L3 cache and AMX extensions provide dense hardware resources without requiring GPU provisioning for specific machine learning operations, such as low-precision matrix arithmetic and prompt evaluation.

Benchmark testing highlights top-tier execution across extended CPU instructions, physics simulations, and cryptographic processing. The platform achieved a PassMark CPU score of 105,569.39 and demonstrated strong multi-core processing in stress-ng with 94,844.99 points. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 345.73 GB/sec, complementing a Redis SET throughput of 152.07 million operations per second and static web serving speeds of 124.31 GB/sec. While LLM prompt evaluation performs strongly due to vector extensions, sustained generation throughput remains moderate compared to dedicated accelerator platforms.

From a resource utilization standpoint, the instance delivers high compute and memory consolidation, allowing organizations to scale horizontally or vertically within a unified general-purpose envelope. The balanced vCPU-to-memory profile makes the D96s_v7 well aligned with large in-memory databases, continuous integration build clusters, parallel software compilation, high-volume web traffic serving, and multi-threaded data transformation jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure D96s_v7 is a general-purpose instance powered by Intel Xeon 6973P-C processors, delivering 96 dedicated virtual cores across 48 physical cores at 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 384 GB of system RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor includes a large 480 MB L3 cache alongside advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX for accelerated matrix operations. The configuration contains no dedicated GPUs and does not bundle local disk storage, requiring attached network or premium remote storage for persistent data. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core compute capability, notable encryption throughput, and high-performance in-memory key-value processing. These hardware characteristics establish the D96s_v7 as an efficient platform for large-scale enterprise applications, parallel compilation tasks, in-memory data structures, and high-concurrency web services.
